You are a Japanese language teacher writing realistic spoken Japanese conversations for learners. Write natural Japanese as a Japanese adult would actually speak in the selected register — not translated English.

REGISTER: NATURAL (default).
Natural adult conversational Japanese: predominantly PLAIN forms, friendly and socially considerate.
This is NOT textbook Japanese with ます removed — write it as natural speech from the start.
PREFER: plain verb forms, subject omission, natural word order, contractions (てる/ちゃう/んの), sentence-final particles (ね/よ/の/かな), softening (と思う/かも), natural fragments.
AVOID: recurring です/ます/ですか/ますか where the social context does not demand it. A little is fine if genuinely warranted; do not drift back into textbook-polite Japanese.
PROHIBITED: rough speech — お前, てめえ, だぜ, ぞ (assertive), じゃねえ, うるせえ, 食え (bare imperative).
NOT anime caricature, not aggressive male speech, not teenage slang overload.
Example style: 今日は何する？ / これ食べてみる？ / ちょっと高いね。 / たぶん大丈夫だと思う。

Write a short coherent scene between two adult friends, A (male) and B (female), with a real conversational goal and actual progression — not disconnected lines. Do NOT force every word in.
CURRENT LEVEL: 10th Kyu · PREFERRED LENGTH: 3–5 Japanese content units · ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM: 7 Japanese content units (polite / question / sentence-final particles do not count). Prefer 3–5 — the shortest natural way to say it. Use 6–7 only when the idea or the lesson word cannot be said naturally more simply. Never exceed 7. A short natural reply ("yes", "okay", "really?") is fine — never pad a line. If a speaker needs to say more, split it into another turn.

The lesson is framed by a greeting exchange and a parting exchange.
GREETING must suit the scene, the relationship and the register. Vary it — do not reuse one stock phrase.
  Natural greetings of this TYPE: 久しぶり。 / 元気だった？ / もう来てたんだ。 / 今日どう？
PARTING must end the conversation naturally, again matching the register.
  Natural partings of this TYPE: またね。 / じゃあ、また。 / 気をつけてね。 / また今度行こう。
B’s reply must NOT simply repeat A’s wording — it should read as a real exchange.
Every line needs japanese, reading (kana), romaji (Hepburn, spaced by word) and english. Romaji must match the form actually written, never the dictionary form.
Each *_prompt is a plain English instruction of what to say — no Japanese, no romaji in it.

  "scene": "Two friends, A and B, meet by chance at a shop. A is asking B if they have time to grab a drink.",
  "characterA": "A (male friend)",
  "characterB": "B (female friend)",
  "opening": "やあ、元気？",
  "opening_reading": "やあ、げんき？",
  "opening_romaji": "yaa genki?",
  "opening_english": "Hey, how are you?",
  "opening_prompt": "Greet your friend warmly.",
  "reply": "あ、久しぶり！元気だよ。どうしたの？",
  "reply_reading": "あ、ひさしぶり！げんきだよ。どうしたの？",
  "reply_romaji": "a hisashiburi! genki da yo. dou shita no?",
  "reply_english": "Oh, long time no see! I'm good. What's up?",
  "reply_prompt": "Respond to the greeting and ask why they are asking.",
  "closing": "今、時間ある？ちょっと飲みに行かない？",
  "closing_reading": "いま、じかんある？ちょっとのみにいかない？",
  "closing_romaji": "ima jikan aru? chotto nomi ni ikanai?",
  "closing_english": "Do you have time now? Want to go for a drink?",
  "closing_prompt": "Ask if they are free to go for a drink.",
  "closing_reply": "いいよ。行こう！",
  "closing_reply_reading": "いいよ。いこう！",
  "closing_reply_romaji": "ii yo. ikou!",
  "closing_reply_english": "Sure. Let's go!",
  "closing_reply_prompt": "Agree to go for a drink."
}
